clue.text: Still cold, wrapped in piece of woollen cloth

parts.note: plaid is a tartan woollen cloth
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone stays motionless in the cold, bundled up in a woollen blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside PLAID to make PLACID.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid and still both describe calm, undisturbed water or a tranquil temperament.

clue.text: Sanctimonious leader of cult in affair, having fling

parts.note: pi is short for pious, i.e. sanctimonious

parts.note: a thing can mean an affair, as in 'they had a thing'

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: A self-righteous cult leader caught up in a scandalous affair.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, the crossword abbreviation of pious, means smugly religious; 'fling' looks like a romance but means a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitching means throwing, and having a fling is throwing something too.

clue.text: Make nothing of a boxer's last round

taken as written

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A boxer's final round is rendered meaningless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a boxing round but is the adjective meaning ring-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Annular means ring-shaped, from the Latin for ring, so circular or round.

clue.text: It's not fair, people being taken in by bad client

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
men are people

explanation.surface: A complaint that people are being conned by a dishonest client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fair' sounds like injustice but refers to weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclement weather is stormy or harsh, the opposite of fair weather.

clue.text: Single out what's central to president if young

indicators.note: the letters wanted lie in the middle of the following words, run together

parts.note: the run of letters inside these three words

explanation.surface: A political commentator picks out a leader who has taken office while young.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify someone is to pick them out or distinguish them from others.

clue.text: With record margin, one people showing good judgment

parts.note: a disc is a record; 'with' joins it on
a rim is an edge or margin
I is the Roman numeral one
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A people who won by a record margin show they choose wisely.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrimination in its older sense is discernment, the ability to judge well between things.

clue.text: Specialised skill, from what we hear? Absolutely not!

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken aloud, so the answer only sounds like the clued phrase

parts.note: know-how is practical expertise

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether they have the expertise flatly refuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Nohow is a dialect or informal word meaning in no way at all.

clue.text: Parts of feet getting hot or cool on flight

parts.note: hot and cool both mean fashionable, i.e. in
a flight is a set of stairs or steps

explanation.surface: Feet get hot or cold on a plane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel; it is a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: The instep is the arched middle part of the foot between toes and ankle.

clue.text: Like dates, with one exception, unknown in advance

parts.note: y is an algebraic unknown
early means ahead of time

explanation.surface: Dates are said to be unknown beforehand, bar one.
explanation.walkthrough: Every calendar date comes round once a year, except 29 February.
explanation.definitionFit: Calendar dates such as birthdays recur annually, and the leap day is the one that does not.

clue.text: Tories are mad about one in Commons following Conservative peers

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this part comes after the opening piece

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the next piece

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
a Member of Parliament sits in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: Conservatives are angry with one of their own MPs who follows the party line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peers' looks like members of the Lords, but means equals of the same age.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemporaries are people living at the same time, one's peers in age.

clue.text: Showing doggedness wrongly put into cause

indicators.note: letters put wrongly are set in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A campaigner stubbornly backs a cause even though the effort is misplaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a link word for 'put into', but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacious means holding on firmly, which is exactly persistent stubbornness or doggedness.

clue.text: Small house by ocean for prophetic writer

parts.note: HO is the short form of house; 'small' signals the abbreviation
a synonym

explanation.surface: A seaside cottage is the home of a writer of prophecies.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is an Old Testament prophet whose book of prophecies bears his name.

clue.text: Like the most sacred thing that is penned by composer

indicators.note: what is penned is enclosed, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Gustav Holst, composer of The Planets
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A sacred piece of music was written by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Gustav Holst is the English composer of The Planets suite.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiest is the superlative of holy, describing whatever is most sacred.

clue.text: Bad treatment for natural wood

parts.note: raw means unprocessed, in its natural state
deal is sawn pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Untreated timber gets rough handling.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a British word for softwood planking.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw deal is an idiom for unfair or harsh handling of someone.

clue.text: Characteristic of courageous person, never being ruffled

indicators.note: ruffled means disturbed or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A brave person is someone who never gets flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve is boldness or courage, the quality that marks a brave person.

clue.text: Prepare to recall note I put in code

parts.note: me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: a thing put in something else is placed inside it

parts.note: Morse is the dot-and-dash code
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy readies a message by encoding a note in cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepare to recall' reads as a whole definition: learning by heart is preparation for recalling later.
explanation.definitionFit: To memorise is to learn something by heart, getting ready to recall it later.

clue.text: Run over revised clues I have separated from others

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: something revised is reworked, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter goes through reworked clues kept apart from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A reclusive person lives in seclusion, cut off from other people.

clue.text: Write label about figure in plan for military HQ

definitions.text: figure in plan for military HQ

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tag is a label
on can mean about, as in 'a book on birds'

explanation.surface: Someone writes a label on a drawing for an army headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pentagon in Virginia is the US Defense Department's headquarters, named for its five-sided ground plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagon is a five-sided figure, and the US military HQ is built in that shape.

clue.text: Tree is what ruined instrument

indicators.note: a ruined thing is broken up, so the preceding word's letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
a horn is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A puzzled cry: a tree is what wrecked the musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The hawthorn is a thorny shrub or small tree, also called may.

clue.text: E.g. sail erratically across river in African capital

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so the jumble goes around the next piece
erratically means without regular order, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A boat zigzags across a river in a North African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Algiers is the capital city of Algeria, on the Mediterranean coast of Africa.

clue.text: Land in South America suffering from cold, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word wanted only sounds like the one clued

parts.note: chilly means feeling cold

explanation.surface: A South American country where people are said to feel the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the country is often said 'chilly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile is a long, narrow country on the Pacific coast of South America.

clue.text: Insinuated rascal spoke dishonestly

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal
to lie is to speak dishonestly

explanation.surface: Someone hinted that a scoundrel had told untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Implied and insinuated both mean suggested indirectly rather than stated.

clue.text: Loathing that's irrelevant without a purpose

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece surrounds the rest

parts.note: N/A, not applicable, is marked against irrelevant items
taken as written
a use is a purpose

explanation.surface: Disgust at something pointless and without any aim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', but here it means outside: N(A USE)A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea can mean strong disgust or revulsion, not just sickness.

clue.text: A regal upset about British subject creating class struggle?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled word surrounds the next piece
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A royal personage is disturbed by a British subject sparking conflict between social classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class struggle' suggests Marx, but it means a school class struggling with its maths; B goes inside LGERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is a branch of mathematics taught at school that many pupils find hard.

clue.text: Part of goal supported by noble

parts.note: the crossbar is part of a goal
in a down entry, a thing supported by another sits on top of it, so ON follows

explanation.surface: An aristocrat props up the frame of a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a member of the lowest rank of the British peerage.

clue.text: Part of brass band behind with note, time after time

T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.walkthrough: RUMP + E + T comes after another T, so 'time after time' gives T at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpet is one of the main instruments in a brass band.

clue.text: Stick fork, say, into small fruit or vegetable, right?

to do is to perform
L is the abbreviation for line
taken as written

clue.text: Top player finishes off the season heavy
